description: Verify that DUT drops an ARP Request whose target_ip is not DUT's own IP — receiver must reply only when the resolution target matches itself (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
The core invariant of ARP_36, restated as a negative. If target_ip belongs to some other host on the same broadcast segment, DUT is not the answer and must stay silent — replying would inject a wrong mapping into the requester's cache.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • opcode      = 1
   • target_ip   = some IP that is NOT DUT's   ← key check
   • sender_*    = HOST-1-IP / MAC-ADDR1

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: no ARP Reply

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_unexpected_reply — DUT replied despite target_ip not being its own. Cache-poisoning class bug — peers would get the wrong MAC-IP binding.

verdicts.Pass: DUT silently dropped the Request — correct rejection
verdicts.Fail_unexpected_reply: DUT replied despite target_ip ≠ DUT IP — cache-poisoning class bug
